note: The advisories the JavaScript dependency gate accepts, each with the reason it is accepted. The gate (scripts/npm-audit-gate.mjs) fails the build on any advisory at or above the level above that is NOT listed here; the advisories below the level are listed as well, so the whole set of known advisories is on the record instead of a number. Every entry names the path the advisory reaches this repository through, the fix - or says there is none - and the reason the risk is accepted.

GHSA-5p2g-fcmc-qvqq.fix: 2.0.3+, but 2.x is not a drop-in: 1.x exports the parser as a callable module (`module.exports = exports = imageSize`), while 2.x's CommonJS build exports a namespace object (`exports.imageSize` / `exports.default`) and metro calls the module as a function. metro pins image-size ^1.0.2, so the fix has to land with the Metro / React Native upgrade that widens that range.
GHSA-5p2g-fcmc-qvqq.reason: Build-time asset sizing. The only images parsed are the repository's own committed assets, so the malformed JXL or HEIF file that triggers the infinite loop has to be committed to the repository - it is not an input the app fetches from anywhere.

GHSA-w3rx-r6r6-pgpr.fix: 2.0.3+, with the same shape change as GHSA-5p2g-fcmc-qvqq: 2.x exports a namespace object instead of the callable module metro calls, and metro pins image-size ^1.0.2.
GHSA-w3rx-r6r6-pgpr.reason: Build-time asset sizing. The only images parsed are the repository's own committed assets, so the malformed ICNS file that triggers the infinite loop has to be committed to the repository.

GHSA-rj75-hqrm-r3gf.fix: 7.1.6+, but both parents pin ^6.1.x and 7.x is a major release of the parser with a different API, so the fix has to land with the Tailwind / postcss-nested upgrade.
GHSA-rj75-hqrm-r3gf.reason: The CSS being parsed is the repository's own stylesheet. The quadratic blow-up needs a selector with an enormous number of flat selectors, in a file the operator wrote.

GHSA-vcc3-ghjq-m6fr.fix: 0.5.0, but that release is ESM-only (`"type": "module"`) and query-string is CommonJS, so the bump breaks the router's dependency chain; there is no 0.4.3 to move to.
GHSA-vcc3-ghjq-m6fr.reason: The decoded string is a deep link's query string. The exponential decoding needs thousands of nested percent escapes in one query parameter.

GHSA-qr28-fpjm-wq7f.fix: 0.5.1, but it is ESM-only (`"type": "module"`) exactly like 0.5.0, and query-string is CommonJS: the require would hand back a namespace object instead of the callable the router invokes, so the bump breaks the router's dependency chain.
GHSA-qr28-fpjm-wq7f.reason: Same package, same path and the same code path as GHSA-vcc3-ghjq-m6fr above: the fallback decoder that only runs when the native decodeURIComponent throws. The input is a deep link's query string and the work happens on the device, in the app's JavaScript runtime, so the twenty-second stall is local to the person who opened a malformed ~224 KB link - it is not reachable from this service, and no server-side endpoint parses URLs through this package.

GHSA-w5hq-g745-h8pq.path: uuid 7.0.3 <- xcode <- @expo/config-plugins (the Expo plugin that edits the iOS Xcode project)
GHSA-w5hq-g745-h8pq.fix: 11.1.1+, but xcode pins uuid ^7.0.3, so 11.x is a major bump.
GHSA-w5hq-g745-h8pq.reason: The vulnerable entry points are uuid's v3, v5 and v6 with a caller-supplied output buffer. xcode calls uuid.v4() only - pbxProject.generateUuid, to mint an object identifier - so the check that the advisory is about never runs.
